context:
Follow existing shared-pattern boundaries:

1) For write-primitives table-existence checks, introduce/reuse a small shared
SQL execution compatibility helper (execute-or-sql fallback) that can be used
by benchmark setup code without encoding DataFusion-specific logic in multiple
call sites. Keep the fallback narrow and deterministic.

2) For read-primitives map queries, implement DataFusion-specific `variants`
SQL in `queries.yaml` rather than broad skips, using syntax validated against
the installed DataFusion SQL dialect. Keep the default query text intact for
other platforms.

3) For concurrent working-dir cleanup, apply the minimum fix around DataFusion
directory delete/recreate paths (lock file or equivalent scoped mutex) and
preserve existing database reuse checks so compatible data is reused rather than
always recreated.

4) Add focused unit/integration regression tests that assert parity behavior
(equivalent execution intent, not necessarily identical timings).
description:
DataFusion runs for `write_primitives` and `read_primitives` are not behaviorally
equivalent to the SQL baseline due to three concrete defects:

1. Write-primitives setup checks call `connection.execute(...)` directly in
   `WritePrimitivesBenchmark._table_exists()` and related setup probes, but
   DataFusion SQL execution uses `SessionContext.sql(...).collect()`.
   This causes false negatives for required TPC-H source table existence and
   aborts most operations before execution.

2. Read-primitives MAP queries (`map_construction`, `map_access`, `map_keys_values`)
   currently use SQL forms that fail on DataFusion parser/planner. These queries
   are still scheduled for DataFusion without a working dialect variant, so
   runs fail despite equivalent intent being possible.

3. Concurrent DataFusion runs targeting the same working directory can race on
   directory removal, producing intermittent `Could not remove existing database`
   failures. This also undermines reliable database reuse decisions.

Goal: restore platform parity so the same benchmark command (SQL mode) performs
the equivalent action on DataFusion, while preserving existing adapter architecture,
shared validation/reuse flow, and avoiding one-off duplicated logic.

anti_patterns.dont: bypass base adapter lifecycle with ad-hoc cleanup in benchmark code
anti_patterns.instead: integrate minimal locking at the adapter boundary
anti_patterns.why: reuse and compatibility checks already live in shared adapter flow

anti_patterns.instead: serialize destructive cleanup only when needed

anti_patterns.dont: hardcode `if platform == datafusion` branches at every write-primitives call site
anti_patterns.instead: centralize execution compatibility in one helper path

anti_patterns.dont: solve map-query failures by globally skipping map category on DataFusion
anti_patterns.instead: add DataFusion variants with validated syntax

preserves.behavior: Base adapter reuse/recreate flow in `benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py` remains the single source of truth for database lifecycle decisions
DataFusion benchmark commands that already pass (for non-map read queries) continue to run without regression
Existing DuckDB/PostgreSQL/SQLite write-primitives setup behavior remains unchanged
Read-primitives catalog variant and skip_on semantics in `benchbox/core/read_primitives/catalog/loader.py` and `benchbox/core/read_primitives/queries.py` remain backward compatible

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/benchmarks/test_write_primitives_core.py -k "table_exists or setup" -v
verifications.description: Write-primitives setup check uses DataFusion-compatible SQL execution path and no longer false-negatives source tables
verifications.expected: targeted write-primitives setup tests pass with no DataFusion API mismatch failures

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/integration/test_read_primitives_datafusion.py -k "map_construction or map_access or map_keys_values" -v
verifications.description: Read-primitives map queries have valid DataFusion SQL variants and execute successfully
verifications.expected: map query integration tests pass on DataFusion

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/integration/test_datafusion_adapter.py -k "concurrent or working_dir or reuse" -v
verifications.description: Concurrent DataFusion run setup no longer fails on working-dir cleanup races
verifications.expected: no intermittent `Could not remove existing database` errors across repeated runs

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m benchbox run --platform datafusion --benchmark write_primitives --scale 1 --non-interactive --phases power
verifications.description: End-to-end parity sanity for both primitive benchmarks on DataFusion SQL mode
verifications.expected: write-primitives runs queries instead of failing setup on missing source tables

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m benchbox run --platform datafusion --benchmark read_primitives --scale 1 --non-interactive --queries map_construction,map_access,map_keys_values --phases power
verifications.description: End-to-end read-primitives map category runs on DataFusion without parser failure
verifications.expected: all three map queries execute or fail only for non-syntax reasons

work_units.summary: Design and add a shared SQL execution compatibility helper that supports DB-API `execute()` and DataFusion `sql(...).collect()` paths
Refactor write-primitives setup/table-existence checks to use the compatibility helper and verify source-table detection on DataFusion
Research DataFusion map SQL syntax and implement dialect `variants` for map_construction/map_access/map_keys_values in read-primitives catalog
Add/adjust read-primitives variant tests to assert DataFusion map variants are selected and executable
Implement minimal concurrency guard for DataFusion working-dir delete/recreate path while preserving base adapter reuse semantics
Add regression tests for DataFusion cleanup race and reuse behavior under repeated/concurrent initialization
Run targeted unit/integration and command-level verification for read/write primitives parity, then document outcomes in TODO item notes
